title: Find out which python3 is running on this Mac
summary: A Mac can have several copies of Python 3: the one that comes with Xcode Command Line Tools, one from Homebrew, and one from python.org. These commands list every copy the Terminal can find and show each version.

aliases.text: what python version is on my mac
which python is running in terminal mac
how many pythons installed on macos
какой python запускается в терминале mac

steps.explain: List every python3 the Terminal can find, in the order it searches them. The first line is the copy that runs when you type python3.
steps.expect: Paths such as /usr/bin/python3 (Xcode tools), /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (Homebrew). Nothing printed means no python3 on PATH.

steps.explain: Show the version of the python3 that runs by default. Note: on a Mac without Command Line Tools, /usr/bin/python3 may open a dialog asking to install them; you can cancel it.
steps.expect: A line like 'Python 3.x.y'. Which copy this is depends on the first path from the previous step.

alternatives.explain: Show the version of one specific copy from the list. Copy a path from the previous step into <PYTHON_PATH>.

placeholders.name: PYTHON_PATH
placeholders.description: A full path to a python3 file, one of the lines printed by 'which -a python3'

alternatives.expect: A line like 'Python 3.x.y' for that exact copy.

source.title: which manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
